algorithms.name: UCB1 (confidence radius sqrt(2 log T / n))

source.label: IID:thm:explore-first
source.quote: Explore-first achieves regret $\E\sbr{R(T)} \leq T^{2/3} \times O(K \log T)^{1/3}$.

results.notes: Textbook result; regret defined via means (pseudo-regret).

source.label: IID:thm:eps-greedy
source.quote: Epsilon-greedy algorithm with exploration probabilities $\eps_t=t^{-1/3} \cdot (K\log t)^{1/3}$ achieves regret bound $\E[R(t)] \leq t^{2/3} \cdot O(K \log t)^{1/3}$ for each round $t$.

results.notes: Holds for each round t; written with T. Proof left as exercise.

source.quote: For two arms, Algorithm~\ref{IID:SE-two} achieves regret $\E\sbr{R(t)} \leq O\rbr{\sqrt{t\log T}}$ for each round $t\leq T$.

results.notes: Stated for every t<=T; recorded at t=T.

source.label: IID:thm:SE-sqrtT

results.notes: Stated for every t<=T; recorded at t=T.

source.label: IID:thm:SE-logT
source.quote: Successive Elimination algorithm achieves regret $\E[R(T)]\leq O(\log{T}) \sbr{ \sum_{\text{arms $a$ with $\mu(a)<\mu(a^*)$}}\frac{1}{\mu(a^*)-\mu(a)} }$.
Algorithm \UcbOne satisfies regret bounds in \eqref{IID:eq:thm:SE-sqrtT} and \eqref{IID:eq:thm:SE-logT}.

results.notes: Book's UCB1 uses log T in confidence radius.

source.quote: Algorithm \UcbOne satisfies regret bounds in \eqref{IID:eq:thm:SE-sqrtT} and \eqref{IID:eq:thm:SE-logT}.

source.label: LB:thm:LB-root-t-basic
source.quote: Fix time horizon $T$ and the number of arms $K$. For any bandit algorithm, there exists a problem instance such that $\E[R(T)]\geq \Omega(\sqrt{KT})$.

results.notes: Originally due to Auer et al. 2002 (bandits-exp3).

conditions: instance chosen uniformly at random from the family I_a

source.label: LB:thm:LB-root-t
source.quote: Fix time horizon $T$ and the number of arms $K$. Fix a bandit algorithm. Choose an arm $a$ uniformly at random, and run the algorithm on problem instance $\mI_a$. Then $\E[R(T)]\geq \Omega(\sqrt{KT})$

bound.regime: T <= c*K/eps^2 for a small absolute constant c, where eps/2 is the gap of instances I_a

conditions: arm a chosen uniformly at random, instance I_a with best arm mean 1/2+eps/2, others 1/2

source.label: LB:cor:MAB-with-predictions
source.quote: Assume $T$ is as in Lemma~\ref{LB:lm:MAB-with-predictions}. Fix any algorithm for ``best-arm identification". Choose an arm $a$ uniformly at random, and run the algorithm on instance $\mI_a$. Then $\Pr[y_T \neq a] \geq \tfrac{1}{12}$

results.notes: Equivalently T >= Omega(K/eps^2) needed. Lemma 28 is the deterministic-algorithm version.

source.label: LB:thm:non-adaptive
source.quote: Consider any algorithm which satisfies non-adaptive exploration. Fix time horizon $T$ and the number of arms $K<T$. Then there exists a problem instance such that $\E[R(T)]\geq \Omega\rbr{T^{2/3}\cdot K^{1/3}}$.

symbols.C_ub: constant C in the algorithm's worst-case guarantee E[R(T)] <= C T^gamma
symbols.gamma_exp: exponent gamma of the algorithm's worst-case guarantee

conditions: algorithm satisfies E[R(T)] <= C T^gamma for all instances

source.label: LB:thm:non-adaptive-refined
source.quote: In the setup of Theorem~\ref{LB:thm:non-adaptive}, suppose $\E[R(T)]\leq C\cdot T^\gamma$ for all problem instances, for some numbers $\gamma\in[\nicefrac23,1)$ and $C>0$. Then for any problem instance a random permutation of arms yields \[ \E\sbr{R(T)} \geq \Omega\rbr{ C^{-2}\cdot T^\lambda\cdot \sum_a \Delta(a)}\]

conditions: prior has finite support; rewards take finitely many values (simplification)

source.label: TS:thm:TS-UB
source.quote: Bayesian Regret of Thompson Sampling is $\BReg(T) = O(\sqrt{KT\log(T)})$.

results.notes: From Russo & Van Roy. Proof uses Hoeffding confidence bounds, so rewards assumed bounded in [0,1].

symbols.c_ALG: absolute constant in base algorithm's guarantee E[R_S(T)] <= c_ALG sqrt(|S| T log T)

conditions: base algorithm ALG satisfies E[R_S(T)] <= c_ALG sqrt(|S| T log T)

source.label: Lip:thm:CAB-uniform
source.quote: Consider continuum-armed bandits with Lipschitz constant $L$ and time horizon $T$. Uniform discretization with algorithm \ALG satisfying \eqref{Lip:eq:opt-regret} and discretization step $\eps=(TL^2/\log T)^{-1/3}$ attains \[ \E[R(T)] \leq L^{1/3}\cdot T^{2/3} \cdot (1+\algC)(\log T)^{1/3}. \]

source.label: Lip:thm:LB-CAB
source.quote: Let \ALG be any algorithm for continuum-armed bandits with time horizon $T$ and Lipschitz constant $L$. There exists a problem instance $\mI=\mI(x^*,\eps)$ ... such that $\E\sbr{ R(T)\mid\mI} \geq \Omega \rbr{L^{1/3}\cdot T^{2/3}}$.

results.notes: Proof given for L=1. Setting uses bounded_01 though instances are Bernoulli.

symbols.d_cov: covering dimension of the metric space with multiplier c
symbols.c_cov: multiplier c of the covering dimension

conditions: base algorithm ALG satisfies E[R_S(T)] <= c_ALG sqrt(|S| T log T)
tuning: eps-mesh S of size O(c/eps^d) with eps=(T/log T)^{-1/(d+2)}

source.label: Lip:thm:LipMAB-unif
source.quote: Consider Lipschitz bandits on a metric space $(X,\mD)$, with time horizon $T$. Let \ALG be any algorithm satisfying \eqref{Lip:eq:opt-regret}. Fix any $c>0$, and let $d=\COV(X)$ be the covering dimension. Then there exists a subset $S\subset X$ such that running $\ALG$ on the set of arms $S$ yields regret $\E[R(T)] \leq (1+\algC)\cdot T^{(d+1)/(d+2)}\cdot (c\,\log T)^{1/(d+2)}$.

results.notes: Constants loosely tracked in the book.

symbols.d_cov: parameter d of metric space ([0,1], l2^{1/d}); its covering dimension

source.label: Lip:thm:LB-CovDim
source.quote: Consider Lipschitz bandits on metric space \CABmetric, for any $d\geq 1$, with time horizon $T$. For any algorithm, there exists a problem instance $\mI$ such that $\E\sbr{R(T)\mid\mI} \geq \Omega\rbr{T^{(d+1)/(d+2)}}$.

symbols.c_zoom: multiplier c of the zooming dimension

conditions: realized rewards take values in a finite set

source.label: Lip:thm:LipMAB-zooming
source.quote: Consider Lipschitz bandits with time horizon $T$. Assume that realized rewards take values on a finite set. For any given problem instance and any $c>0$, the zooming algorithm attains regret $\E[R(T)] \leq O\rbr{ T^{(d+1)/(d+2)}\; (c\log T)^{1/(d+2)}}$, where $d$ is the zooming dimension with multiplier $c$.

conditions: there exists a perfect expert who never makes a mistake

source.label: FF:thm:perfect-expert
source.quote: Consider binary prediction with experts advice. Assuming a perfect expert, the majority vote algorithm makes at most $\log_2 K$ mistakes, where $K$ is the number of experts.

source.label: FF:thm:binary-prediction-LB
source.quote: Consider binary prediction with experts advice. For any algorithm, any $T$ and any $K$, there is a problem instance with a perfect expert such that the algorithm makes at least $\Omega(\min(T,\log K))$ mistakes.

results.notes: Number of mistakes; probability type not stated (deterministic/expected).

source.label: FF:thm:WMA
source.quote: The number of mistakes made by WMA with parameter $\eps\in(0,1)$ is at most $\frac{2}{1 - \eps} \cdot \cost^* + \frac{2}{\eps} \cdot \ln{K}$.

results.notes: Bounds number of mistakes; L_star = cost* (mistakes of best expert).

symbols.u_cost: known number u with cost* <= uT (trivially u=1)

source.label: FF:thm:hedge-main
source.quote: Assume all costs are at most $1$. Consider an adaptive adversary such that $\cost^*\leq uT$ for some known number $u$; trivially, $u=1$. Then \Hedge with parameter $\eps=\sqrt{\tfrac{\ln K}{uT}}$ satisfies \[ \E[\cost(\ALG)-\cost^*] < 2\cdot \sqrt{uT \ln{K}}.\]

results.notes: Regret against best-observed (in-hindsight) arm under adaptive adversary.

source.quote: Ensuring that $\eps T = \frac{K}{\eps}\log{T}$ yields ... and therefore $R(T) \le O\rbr{\sqrt{KT\log T}}$.

results.notes: Alternative derivation of Theorem 14; duplicate of r4 essentially.

source.quote: Using the same parameters, $\alpha=\eps=\sqrt{\tfrac{\ln K}{T}}$ and $\beta=0$, and assuming all costs are at most $1$, \refeq{FF:eq:raw} implies that $\sum_{t\in [T]} p_t\cdot c_t -\cost^* < 2 \cdot \sqrt{T \ln{K}}$.

results.notes: Holds with probability 1 for the expected per-round cost p_t.c_t.
